poems.title: How to Win My Heart
poems.note: Thames St at Broadway — the corner café at the Harbor of the Heavens

set_pieces.name: Walk from the temple around the harbor
set_pieces.line: 13 HOW TO WIN MY HEART · A Walk from the temple around the harbor — “with every pulsing beat after walking alone”

set_pieces.name: The corner cafe table
set_pieces.line: 13 HOW TO WIN MY HEART · B The corner cafe table — “I want you to notice me in a corner cafe”

set_pieces.name: Distances, younger selves, praying elders
set_pieces.line: 13 HOW TO WIN MY HEART · C Distances, younger selves, praying elders — “with the distances we couldn't avoid”

set_pieces.name: Victory-less seasons (inner montage)
set_pieces.line: 13 HOW TO WIN MY HEART · D Victory-less seasons (inner montage) — “I've journeyed beyond any place you can conceivably

set_pieces.name: Harvesting the poppies
set_pieces.line: 13 HOW TO WIN MY HEART · E Harvesting the poppies — “harvest a wizardry more brilliant”

set_pieces.name: From a distant window
set_pieces.line: 13 HOW TO WIN MY HEART · F From a distant window — “Yet from a distant window, beautiful and calm”

set_pieces.name: Stands and walks the harbor
set_pieces.line: 13 HOW TO WIN MY HEART · G Stands and walks the harbor — “all the fatigue of wandering alone in thought”

foundry_refs.desc: POET rises from the café table and begins walking along the harbor.
POET is still at the café, continuing to observe the romantic couples from a distance.
Literal visual match: Man in tracksuit with clear plastic sleeves walking with stepped multi-exposure echo trail.
foundry_refs.line: Then, a distant window. She says: you'll see me. Capture the eyes. Refocus. Step back. Say hello. Don't make me leave. I escaped here for a reason.
